chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who has four wives and he divorces one, adding another to her; he said: 'No, until the waiting period expires.' I said: 'Who observes the waiting period?' He said: 'He.' I said: 'Even if it is a temporary marriage (mut'ah)?' He said: 'Even if it is a temporary marriage.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on replacing a wife in a four-wife marriage or temporary marriage according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the procedural requirement for a man managing four wives who wishes to replace one with another: he must wait for the specific divorced wife's 'iddah to expire before the new marriage is fully consummated or recognized in the count. This ruling underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in maintaining the limit of four simultaneous marriages, ensuring that the 'iddah of the departing wife is strictly observed before the incoming wife's status is fully integrated, a principle that extends even to temporary marriage (mut'ah).
